content: Swelling of the lymph nodes, face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat can occur. Difficulty swallowing or a sensation of tightness in the throat may also be experienced. Skin reactions such as itching, rashes, or pale red bumps known as hives are possible. Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, stomach cramps, and joint pain are additional symptoms that may arise. Precautions: Who Should Not Use Omeprazole? 1. Allergies to Ingredients: Individuals allergic to omeprazole, Prilosec, Prilosec OTC, other proton pump inhibitors, or any specific ingredients in the product should avoid using omeprazole. Pharmacists can provide a detailed list of ingredients in the specific product. 2. Drug Interactions: Omeprazole should not be taken with certain medications. Before starting omeprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. Refer to the interactions section for more details. Important Information Before Using Omeprazole: Only take omeprazole if prescribed by a healthcare provider and follow the prescribed dosage. Do not share omeprazole with others, even if they have similar symptoms, as it may harm them. Keep omeprazole out of reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush omeprazole capsules. Take them before meals. If swallowing capsules is difficult, the contents can be sprinkled on one tablespoon of applesauce and swallowed immediately without mixing with other foods. Omeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to take full effect. What to Tell Your Healthcare Provider Before Using Omeprazole: Inform your provider about all health conditions and medications, including prescription, over-the-counter, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements. Discuss any history of low blood potassium (hypokalemia), low magnesium (hypomagnesemia), low calcium (hypocalcemia), or liver problems. Omeprazole may interact with other medications and supplements, so provide a complete list of what you are taking. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: The effects of omeprazole on pregnancy and unborn babies are not fully known. Inform your provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Do not take omeprazole while breastfeeding, as it can pass into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Take omeprazole before meals. The effects of alcohol on omeprazole are unknown. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications and supplements you are using, especially if you are taking clopidogrel (Plavix), cilostazol (Pletal), citalopram, methotrexate, digoxin (Lanoxin), warfarin, certain antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir), St. John’s Wort, or rifampin. Some medications may alter omeprazole levels in the blood or vice versa. Overdose: If you or someone else has taken too much omeprazole, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one as scheduled. Do not double doses. Uses of Omeprazole: Omeprazole is used to treat heartburn and conditions caused by excess stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and Helicobacter pylori infections. It may also be used for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Omeprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. How Omeprazole is Supplied: Omeprazole is available as Prilosec, Prilosec OTC, and generic forms in various dosage forms, including capsules, tablets, and powder for oral suspension. Storage: Store omeprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). Keep it in a cool, dry place. Common Side Effects: Common side effects include headache, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, gas, and, in children aged 1 to 16, infections in the nose or throat and fever. Contact your healthcare provider if these side effects bother you. Serious Side Effects: 1. Kidney Problems: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis may occur. Seek medical attention if you notice reduced urine output or blood in your urine. 2. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can cause watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your provider immediately if these symptoms occur. 3. Severe Skin Reactions: Rare but serious conditions like Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) can occur. Stop omeprazole and seek emergency help if you develop painful red or purple skin, peeling skin, flat red rashes, blisters, or red, watery eyes. 4. Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS): This severe allergic reaction can affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Stop the medication and seek immediate help. 5. Lupus: Omeprazole may cause or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder. Notify your provider if you experience new or worsening joint pain or a rash on your arms or cheeks. 6. Vitamin B-12 Deficiency: Long-term use (3 years or more) may reduce vitamin B-12 absorption, leading to symptoms like a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling in the hands or feet. 7. Hypomagnesemia: Low magnesium levels can cause seizures, heart rhythm problems, dizziness, or muscle spasms. This risk is higher with long-term use or when combined with other medications that lower magnesium. 8. Bone Loss and Fractures: Long-term or high-dose use may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults. 9. Severe Allergic Reactions: Symptoms include breathing difficulties, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, facial swelling, throat tightness, itching, rash, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or joint pain. Stop omeprazole and seek emergency care if these occur.
